clue.text: This restricts all hair and feathers

parts.note: a lock is a tress or curl of hair
down is the soft fine feathers of a bird

explanation.surface: A description of something that controls every bit of hair and plumage, like a styling product.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockdown is an order confining everyone in a population to their homes or premises, restricting every person at once.

clue.text: In case of love, it hurts being sordid

indicators.note: In places the cry of pain inside the shell taken from the other word
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of love
ouch is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: Being sleazy is painful when you are in love.
explanation.walkthrough: OUCH sits inside L...E, giving L(OUCH)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche describes someone or something disreputable and of dubious morals, close in sense to sordid and seedy.

clue.text: Tip of stiletto knife plunged into hair stylist? That's getting to be expensive

indicators.note: plunging a blade into something drives it inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: a comb styles hair; the question mark admits the stretch

indicators.note: the tip of a blade is its far end, so the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of stiletto
to knife someone is to stab them

explanation.surface: A knife attack on a hairdresser, with the cost of it all mounting.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip of a stiletto is its far end, hence its last letter. To cost a bomb is British slang for to be very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase means to be very pricey, a bomb being slang for a large sum of money.

clue.text: Instrument the wrong way round for this game

indicators.note: wrong way round means the word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: Someone plays an instrument back to front as part of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game where players throw small weighted arrows at a circular board.

clue.text: Amongst clothing, article usually chosen to suit this

definitions.text: Amongst clothing, article usually chosen to suit this

indicators.note: amongst sets one word in the middle of the clothing word

parts.note: wear is clothing, as in menswear
the definite article

explanation.surface: People generally pick their clothes according to conditions outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue says clothing is usually chosen to suit the answer, so the entire clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: We dress for rain, sun or cold, so outdoor conditions are what clothing is usually picked to match.

clue.text: Paramour leaves in the morning, creating turmoil

indicators.note: creating suggests making something new, so the remaining letters are reworked into fresh order
to leave is to depart, so the morning's letters go out of the lover's name

parts.note: taken as written
a.m. is the standard abbreviation for the morning hours

explanation.surface: A lover slips away at dawn, leaving a domestic upheaval behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AM from PARAMOUR leaves PAROUR, whose six letters rearrange to UPROAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud public disturbance or commotion, a synonym for turmoil and confusion.

clue.text: Doctor said champagne here in Paris a non-starter

indicators.note: said tells us to use how the word sounds rather than its spelling

parts.note: fizz is slang for champagne, and the start of the medical word sounds the same
ici is French for here
taken as written

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of non

explanation.surface: A doctor orders champagne in Paris, but nothing comes of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-starter' looks like a description meaning a failure, but it splits into the word non and its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician is a medical doctor, especially one practising general medicine rather than surgery.

clue.text: Disrobe sexily, only a bit overweight

indicators.note: only a bit means just a fragment of the phrase is taken, sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A striptease that reveals a little of a heavy body.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very fat, carrying excess body weight to a medically unhealthy degree.

clue.text: Fuel producer from reef oddly given regalia

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in the first, third and other odd positions

parts.note: the first and third letters of reef
finery is elaborate ceremonial dress, like regalia

explanation.surface: A coral reef is strangely dressed up in ceremonial robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery processes crude oil into petrol and other fuels, so it is a plant that produces fuel.

clue.text: Maps, true to form, showing where water comes from

indicators.note: putting letters into form means shaping them into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Accurate maps reveal the source of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows down from its source, so the water reaching any point has come from the higher stretch above it.

clue.text: Goliath starts to make you see a creature of legend

indicators.note: the starts of the following words means only their opening letters are taken

parts.note: the initial letters of these three words
an elf is a small mischievous being of folklore

explanation.surface: The biblical giant appears to conjure up a mythical creature for you to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: Goliath is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter speaking of himself says the word for the speaker's own self.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters use their pseudonym to mean the first person, and the setter would call himself by the reflexive pronoun.

clue.text: Measure briefly the outline of thumb strap

indicators.note: an outline is the outer edge, so only the first and last letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of thumb
the first and last letters of strap

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up the shape of a thumb strap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' belongs to the definition: the answer is the abbreviation for tablespoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbsp is the short form of tablespoon, a unit of volume used in cooking recipes.

clue.text: Warms up for qualifiers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: raises the temperature of something
second meaning: preliminary races deciding who goes through to the final

explanation.surface: An athlete limbers up before the preliminary rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means makes something warmer, and the plural noun names early rounds of a competition that whittle down entrants.

clue.text: Scottish woman about to get married first to appear in her type of party

indicators.note: in tells us these pieces sit inside the party word

parts.note: a hen party is the celebration held for a woman before her wedding
a bride is a woman on the point of being wed

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the opening letter of appear

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be from Scotland shows up at her own hen night.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is the British pre-wedding celebration for a bride and her friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are Scottish islands, and a Hebridean is a native of them; here it is used for a woman from there.

clue.text: Heartless inquisitor here in Hyde Park?

indicators.note: without a heart means the very middle letter of the word is cut out

parts.note: a coroner holds inquests, inquiring into sudden deaths

explanation.surface: A merciless interrogator is found in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner in Hyde Park, London, is where anyone may stand and harangue the public. Dropping the central O of CORONER gives CORNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Speakers' Corner is a famous spot in Hyde Park, so this word names that place; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Uncle Tom ran out leaving me in the dark

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or wrong
leaving means departing, so the letters of the pronoun are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Uncle Tom ran off and abandoned the speaker in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M and E from UNCLETOMRAN; the nine letters left rearrange to NOCTURNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal means happening or active at night, during the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Rope artist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a line at the bow of a small boat used to tie it up
second meaning: someone who makes pictures with brush and colour

explanation.walkthrough: The nautical sense is the one most solvers don't know: a painter is the mooring line on a dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call the mooring line on a small boat by this name, and it is also the ordinary word for someone who makes pictures.

clue.text: Hard work made out in song

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the song word

parts.note: a trill is a warbling birdsong

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Toil turned into a work song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out' reads as 'discerned', but out is the anagram signal working on made alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is monotonous, tiring work, from the old mill wheel that prisoners were forced to walk.

clue.text: Vegetable producer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a green vegetable with flowering heads
second meaning: Albert 'Cubby' ..., producer of the James Bond films

explanation.walkthrough: 'Vegetable producer' reads as a farmer or market gardener, but it is two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The green vegetable shares its name with Cubby Broccoli, the film producer behind the Bond franchise.

clue.text: No coming back after this massage picture

parts.note: a rub is a massage
an icon is an image, especially a religious painting

explanation.surface: After a session of massage and pictures, there is no going back.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar crossed the river Rubicon in 49 BC, committing himself to civil war; the name now stands for a point of no return.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the river was an irrevocable act, so the name now means a point beyond which retreat is impossible.

clue.text: Gaslighting

parts.note: surface reading: psychological manipulation that makes a victim doubt their own sanity
setter's reading: split it as gas plus lighting, an inert gas that glows in illuminated signs

explanation.walkthrough: The modern word for manipulation splits into a gas and a lighting use.
explanation.definitionFit: This noble gas glows red-orange when electricity passes through it, so it is used for bright advertising signs.

clue.text: National chief in this country on board plane for this?

definitions.text: National chief in this country on board plane for this?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, and on board places them within the aircraft too

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft
the setter writes for a British paper, so this country is the United Kingdom

indicators.note: chief means head, so only the opening letter of the word before is used

parts.note: the opening letter of National

explanation.surface: A country's leader boards a plane at home, and the clue asks what such a trip is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter writes for a British paper, so 'this country' is the UK. Read whole, the clue describes a leader's jaunt abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A junket is a trip or excursion taken by an official at public expense, like a leader flying off on a jaunt.

clue.text: No water or soda, to be fair

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: what you ask for when a whisky should come with only ice

definitions.note: the phrase stands for fairness, a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: fairness, the quality of being fair

explanation.surface: At a bar someone declines any mixer, just to be fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as JUST ICE: a drink with no water or soda added.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice means fairness and impartial treatment, the quality of being fair to all parties.

clue.text: New enemy pursued by one Arab

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fresh foe is being chased by a lone Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a person from Yemen, a country on the Arabian peninsula, so an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: Drunken rubbish, you say, soul-destroying

indicators.note: to destroy something is to wreck its form, so the letters are smashed and remade

parts.note: crap is slang for worthless stuff

indicators.note: say asks us to take the word before as it is pronounced, not written

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the pronoun
the four letters of soul, rearranged

explanation.surface: A rant about drink: you call it rubbish, and it destroys the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulous is a rare adjective meaning suffering the effects of heavy drinking, or given to excessive drinking.

clue.text: Live bear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dwell or reside somewhere
second meaning: to tolerate or put up with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Live bear' looks like an animal in the wild; both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb can mean to dwell somewhere, in an old sense, and also to tolerate, as in cannot stand something.

clue.text: It should hit rock bottom by shore

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of rock
the shore is the edge of the sea

explanation.surface: Something meant to sink to the seabed just off the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also paints the answer in action, since this kind of object is dropped to the sea floor near the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A kedge is a small anchor; 'It' is a bare pointer that the rest of the clue fleshes out as something sinking to the seabed.

clue.text: What bakers do naked is shocking

indicators.note: something shocked is jolted, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bakers working in the nude would be a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers work dough with their hands, pressing and folding it to develop the gluten.

clue.text: Expert knows his roots

definitions.note: completes the idiom 'knows his onions', so the phrase points to its missing last word
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that completes the British idiom for being an expert
second meaning: bulb vegetables that grow underground

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'to know your onions' means to be expert in something; the clue reads as a specialist knowing the origins of his subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for expertise ends with this word, and these bulbs grow below ground like root vegetables.

clue.text: Function as shopkeeper, it's a hobby

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a secondary range of goods a shop stocks alongside its main trade
second meaning: an occupation pursued in addition to one's main job

explanation.surface: Running a shop is just something done for fun on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers an extra line of merchandise in retail and a secondary pastime or job outside one's main work.

clue.text: Ladies can be models of perfection

indicators.note: can be suggests these letters could become something else once reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Women may serve as role models of flawless conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards or examples regarded as perfect, held up for others to aim at or imitate.

clue.text: City I held?

parts.note: the question mark flags a reverse clue: the letters before it are a new version of a city name
taken as written; these letters are the city's name rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they once held a city.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: 'I held' is what you get from a NEW arrangement of DELHI, so the answer describes the clue's own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital of India, a city laid out by the British in the early twentieth century.
